sections.content:
49,615 people

were counted on the census as "dental nurses" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Dental nurses prepare patients for, and assist with, dental examinations, prepare and sterilise instruments and maintain case records.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "dental nurses" there were more women than men (97.4% compared with 2.6%).

This means "dental nurses" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 2.5% and women made up 97.5% of "dental nurses"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "dental nurses" included:

  • early education and childcare assistants
  • early education and childcare practitioners
  • registered children's nurses

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "dental nurses", 17.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "dental nurses" was 65 years or older.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "dental nurses" included:

  • early education and childcare practitioners
  • early education and childcare assistants
  • advertising and marketing associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "dental nurses" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of women than men with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "dental nurses" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "dental nurses", 6.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (61.5% compared with 38.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.1%) than self-employed (1.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
